source.title: DIME: Scaling Facial Representation Learning via Differential Masked Autoencoding
source.authors: Hao Yu; Hao-Yu Chen; Hui Wei; Yan Jiang; N. Sebe; Guo-Ying Zhao

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling laws and reports a visual-pretraining data-scaling experiment, but it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or test the language-model scaling-law versions. Its image-scaling results use downstream AU F1, a different measure from the power-law loss named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. and says scaling laws assume an objective that continues to extract signal from more data. It reports Face-20M data scaling results for MAE-B and DIME-B on BP4D AU F1. These are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the claim versions: they do not report held-out pretraining loss or fit power laws. Other model comparisons and task results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. It is a facial self-supervised pretraining method paper on vision encoders, not language models. Its only scaling result is downstream BP4D AU F1 for MAE-B and DIME-B pretrained on 6M–20M facial images, a range of about 3x. It measures no held-out pretraining loss and fits no power law. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only in the Limitations discussion, saying scaling laws assume an objective that keeps extracting signal. That makes this an objective-dependent downstream scaling observation, not a test of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors report that MAE-B gains about 0.5 F1 from 6M to 20M images while DIME-B gains 5.9. They conclude that scale amplifies the objective rather than replacing it, and expect DIME to saturate once within-identity variation is exhausted. They also note diminishing returns from model size and leave a joint scaling study to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales visual pretraining data and measures downstream facial-task performance; it does not reproduce language-model held-out-loss scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling outcome differs between the MAE and DIME objectives. The authors also state that DIME's effective scale depends on variation diversity and that model scaling has diminishing returns.

fits_no_version.finding: Over 6M to 20M facial pretraining images, BP4D AU F1 for MAE-B rises from 64.5% to about 65.0%. For DIME-B it rises from 66.1% to 72.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In facial-image SSL, downstream gains from more pretraining data depend strongly on the pretraining objective: MAE plateaus while a differential objective keeps improving.

fits_no_version.finding: Model-size scaling of DIME (23M/86M/307M) gives BP4D F1 of 69.8/72.0/73.2, so gains diminish (+2.2, then +1.2). The authors call these diminishing returns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For facial SSL encoders, downstream AU F1 gains from encoder size shrink across the S/B/L sizes.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (identified in the paper header)
record.problems: The scaling comparison reports downstream AU F1 rather than held-out pretraining loss; uncertainty for the reported scaling values is not stated. The scaling sweep is over facial-image data from 6M to 20M images, not several orders of magnitude.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted under the 60-row limit. Task benchmarks and ablations not bearing on the listed scaling-law versions are not included.

untested.parts: No language-model loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Image pretraining data is scaled only over 6M–20M, measured by downstream F1. No pretraining loss and no power-law form are reported.
There are downstream gains with data and model size, but only for vision encoders. No predictive relation to scale or loss is fit.
No exponents are fitted and no fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only in the Limitations section. The model-size results (Tables 2–7) are downstream task metrics across three encoder sizes and do not bear on the loss-based versions.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out loss scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of larger runs are evaluated.
No compute-budget allocation between model parameters and training tokens is evaluated.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count is reported as a test of loss.
The study reports image-pretraining data scaling using downstream AU F1, not whether held-out pretraining loss follows the same power-law form in image models or other training regimes.
No downstream-task performance is related to language-model scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, or sensitivity of such fits to setup or fitting choices are evaluated.
